summary: This bill establishes an alternative maximum tax rate for low- and middle-income individuals based on a cost-of-living exemption and imposes a new surcharge on high-income individuals, both effective for tax years beginning after December 31, 2025.

scores.thoughts: This bill primarily deals with changes to the tax code, specifically reducing taxes for low- and middle-income individuals and increasing them for high-income individuals. It does not directly appropriate funds or authorize new government programs, so its impact on government spending is indirect through potential changes in revenue.

The bill directly amends the Internal Revenue Code to create an alternative maximum tax for low- and middle-income individuals, effectively reducing their tax burden, and imposes a new surcharge on high-income individuals, increasing their taxes. This is a central component of the bill.

While the bill significantly alters tax revenues by both decreasing taxes for some and increasing them for others, it does not explicitly address the national debt or prioritize debt reduction. Its net effect on revenue, and thus indirectly on the national debt, is not specified or its primary focus.
